steps.note: S1.1.1.1 traces rows 0-7 with initial scratch a,c (subtract Ja+Rc, change to a+Vx, c+Gx, add R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx), restore a,c) and concludes the net change (JV+RG)x for every a,c, quoting line 748.
S1.1.1.2 states the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, that side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one pairs, that intersections 0 and 2 already give 0, and that S=T gives 1.

The plan treats only the bit case; the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 and its cancellation by side wires at intersections zero and two appear nowhere (S1.1.3.1's <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1 is the label form, not this coefficient).
S1.1.1.3 gives the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) and says each invocation restores its own scratch wires, quoting line 762.

The plan says every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels (S1.1.3.3) and that rank equals dimension change (S1.1.3.6), but never gives the per-edge orthogonal residuals and their dimensions that make up the residual table.

S1.1.3.2 states the inclusion P(x)<t_X> in P(x)t_Y^perp made possible by t_X perp t_Y (quoting the label assignment at line 953), but not the side edge 2->5 residual <t_X,t_Y>^perp or its dimension h-2, so only half the defining content is there.
S1.1.3.3 names center 3->4 as the only decreasing edge with loss h (L=Ich), and S1.1.3.4 telescopes to sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N and absolute Wm-2N+2L.

The plan uses an orthonormal basis of each residual (S2.1, S2.1.1) but never argues that over F_2 each nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating, or that alternating planes can be absorbed.
S1.1.3.5 gives L_b/N=100/539 and S2.1.2 gives L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.
S2.1.1 states that orthogonal binary vectors have supports meeting evenly, so weight is additive mod 4 and q_V-q_U=sum_v wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal basis of E.

S2.1.1 asserts that each odd-weight v contributes aI+bX_v or its inverse, but gives neither the phase i^{eps[v.x]} nor the identity H diag(1,-1) H = X that turns the diagonal character into a translation, so it asserts the result without the step.

S2.1.3 says each residual basis vector costs exactly one forward child C^{(x)f} on the f axes (columns) of one slot, and S2.1.5 sums these to exactly s_c child calls, matching the one-factor-per-residual-vector, s_c-in-all content as the paper applies it at 1905.

S2.1.5 and S2.1's method name the repairs (endpoint Z signs, scalar i^{27f}, C=iZC^{-1}Z, negating X outputs), but not the endpoint frames I and C^{(x)m} or the C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) that these repairs correct.
S1.1.3.5 gives L_b/N<1/2 and S1.1.3.6 derives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, short of W_b m by N-2L_b>0.
S1.1.4 states the relative deficit (W_b m-s_b)/(W_b m)=339/22587335000000.
The plan gives the complex deficit only as 2N-2L_c>0 (S2.1.2) and never states eta_c=73/19906842167500.

S1.1.4 states that the deficit exceeds 20*2^-50 and that log m<20 gives m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50), so s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^-50; the complex case enters through the quoted 'Both exact deficits' and through S5.1.1's tau=sigma.

S1.1.5.1 states A=E_1 Pi E_2 with Pi having exactly a ones, found by elimination pivoting on the rightmost entry of the topmost nonzero row; the lower-triangular clearing and the repetition on active indices are compressed into 'eliminating'.

S1.1.5's claim has only a parenthetical ('q a fixed prime avoiding all denominators'); the plan never says that the factorization identities, from a finite table, specialize to Z/q^b with the triangular factors still invertible.
S1.1.5.2 states that a lower-triangular transformation of H or D costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order with controlled shifts from earlier, still-original coordinates.
S1.1.5.3 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j, which yields (h+d,d) with one interchange, so the number of recursive calls is exactly a.
S2.5 and S5.1.1 mention C_0 d^{C_1}, C_1=20 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}), but never define E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu or C_0=128mB^2, so the constants are named without their content.
The plan has no arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with leaf bound 8e, or a per-invocation count below E; S2.5 just asserts the depth bound C_0 d^{C_1}.
The unrolling B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu, A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} and the total below C_0 d^{C_1} are absent; the plan states only the final bound.

S2.5 states that a depth-j value lies in 2^{-(p+j)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^j, so p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits hold every value exactly with Delta=o(p); S5.1.1 supplies epsilon*C_1<1.
S2.6 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved, and that the single truncation errs by less than sqrt2*2^-p.

summary: P04 states 15 of 26 sub-steps. It covers the bit-case scalar motif (B1, B2, B4), the label dimension accounting (L3, L5), the core of the phase interface (P1, P3), the bit rank deficit and exponent (R1, R2, R4), most of the matrix shear (M1, M3, M4), and the guard-bit representation and final truncation (S4, S5). It omits the complex-case coefficients (B3), the residual table and nonalternating bases (L1, L4), the side-edge residual of dimension h-2 (L2, only its inclusion is given), the Hadamard step to translation kernels (P2), the endpoint frame computation (P4, only the repairs are named), eta_c (R3), the specialization to Z/q^b (M2), and the guard-width constants, recurrence and unrolling (S1-S3). No sub-step is stated contrary to the paper.
